539:
All accumulations of refuse and trash shall be stored or placed for collection in accordance with the following provisions:
(1) Public streets and private property. No person shall place any accumulations of refuse or trash in any street, median strip, alley or other public place of travel, nor upon any private property except as stated in this article.
(2) Blockage of storm drains. No person shall place any refuse, trash, refuse receptacles or containers on, upon or over any storm drain, or so close thereto as to be drawn by the elements into such storm drain.
(3) Unauthorized accumulations. Any accumulation of refuse or trash items on any lot, property, premises, public street, alley or other public or private place not permitted by this article, is declared to be a public nuisance and is prohibited. Failure of the owner or occupant to remove and correct any such accumulation of refuse shall be deemed a violation of this article.
(4) Junk. It shall be unlawful for any person to place or leave outside any building or dwelling any dilapidated furniture, appliance, machinery, equipment, building material, junked motor vehicle, or other item which is either in a wholly or partially rusted, wrecked, junked, dismantled or inoperative condition, and which is not completely enclosed within a building or dwelling. Any such item or items which remain on the property of the occupant for a period of ten days after notice of violation of this subsection shall be presumed to be abandoned and subject to being removed from the property by the county without further notice. This shall not apply to authorized junk dealers or currently licensed establishments engaged in the repair, rebuilding, reconditioning or salvaging of equipment or furniture.
(5) Appliances. It shall be unlawful for any person to leave outside any building in a place accessible to children any appliance, refrigerator or other container of any kind which has an airtight snap lock or similar device without first removing the lock or door from such appliance, refrigerator or container which has been placed on or adjacent to the rear of the building and is crated, strapped or locked to such an extent that it is impossible for a child to obtain access to any airtight compartment thereof.
(6) Scavenging. No person, other than the owner thereof, or an agent or employee of the director of community development, shall interfere with any container placed for the purpose of storing refuse pending collection, or remove or take any of the contents thereof, or remove any such container from the location where the container shall have been placed by the owner thereof.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 1.8)
540:
(a) Bulk container. Any commercial establishment that furnishes and maintains a bulk container suitable for handling by county equipment will be serviced by the county as stated in this article, provided that such container shall be of sufficient size as specified and be approved for collection. The containers shall at all times be kept clean, neat, painted and in a good state of repair. Service shall be discontinued to establishments failing to maintain containers appropriately. Establishments utilizing bulk containers are responsible for repairing the containers for service. No service shall be given to those establishments permitting objects, obstruction or vehicles to hinder in any way the servicing of the container. Cleaning up spilled materials shall be the responsibility of the property owner or occupant.
(b) Holidays. Collections shall not be made on the following holidays unless otherwise specified by the county administrator: New Year's Day, Fourth of July, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day.
(c) Industrial waste. Industrial waste shall be collected, removed and disposed of by the operator of the factory, plant or enterprise creating or causing such waste.
(d) Hazardous refuse. No hazardous refuse shall be placed in any receptacle used for collection of refuse by the county.
(e) Building materials. The county shall not be responsible for the collecting or hauling of building materials originating from private property preliminary to, during or subsequent to the construction of new buildings, alterations or additions to existing buildings of whatever type or from demolition of existing structures. Such material shall be removed by the owner of the property or by the contractor.
(f) Hazardous, liquid or highly combustible industrial waste. Hazardous waste, liquid waste or highly combustible industrial waste shall not be disposed of in the Cordele-Crisp County Landfill.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 1.15)
541:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to:
(1) Throw or deposit any refuse into any public or private street or scatter refuse about or litter any public or private street, alley, or area or place.
(2) Throw or deposit any refuse, trash or debris in any stream, stream bed or body of water.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any vehicle transporting loose materials within the county to transport such materials without suitable covers. This subsection shall not apply to the transportation of poultry or livestock or silage or other feed grain used in the feeding of poultry or livestock.
(c) Any material that cannot be self-contained in a vehicle by its own weight, other than vegetation, i.e., pinestraw, leaves, etc., will be deemed litter and will be considered a violation of subsection (b) of this section.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 1.9)
542:
(a) It shall be unlawful to place in or on any automobile in the county any handbill, circular, pamphlet, poster, postcard or other literature, except with the express permission of the owner or occupant of such automobile.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to place on private property any handbill, circular, pamphlet, poster, postcard or other literature, except with the express permission of the owner of the property or intended recipient. This subsection shall not apply to multipage printed publications.
(c) It shall be unlawful for any person to tack, post or nail any paper, metal, wood or other signs for advertising material of any character on any telegraph, telephone or electric light pole on any street or alley within the county.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 1.10)
543:
All commercial establishments shall store their refuse in containers as specified in this article so as to eliminate wind-driven debris and unsightly litter in and about their establishments. Approved methods of containerization include refuse receptacles, bulk containers and detachable containers. Spillage and overflow shall be immediately cleaned up by such establishment when and as it occurs.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 1.11)
Cross reference— Businesses, ch. 22.
544:
All loading and unloading areas shall be provided with refuse receptacles for loose debris, paper, packaging materials and other trash. The number of containers necessary for each area shall be as required to maintain clean, neat and sanitary premises as directed by the county administrator. The owner of the premises and the occupant thereof shall jointly and severally maintain surveillance to ensure that all litter is placed in the proper container and the area is kept clean.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 1.12)
Cross reference— Traffic and vehicles, ch. 62.
545:
(a) Obligation to furnish receptacles. All parking lots and establishments with parking lots shall provide refuse receptacles distributed within the parking area. The county administrator shall have the authority to determine the number and types of receptacles necessary to provide proper containerization. Such receptacles shall be weighted or attached to the ground as necessary to prevent spillage. It shall be the responsibility of the owner or the manager of the parking lot to collect the refuse and trash deposited in such containers and store this material in an approved location.
(b) Obligation to use receptacles. It shall be the obligation of all persons using the parking areas to use such refuse receptacles or containers as provided for in subsection (a) of this section for the purpose intended, and it shall be unlawful for any person or persons to dump, scatter or throw upon any such parking lot any refuse, garbage or trash of any kind.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 1.13)
546:
All construction and demolition contractors shall provide onsite refuse receptacles, bulk containers or detachable containers for loose debris, paper, building material waste, scrap building materials and other trash produced by those working on the site. The site shall be kept in a litter-free condition. The number of refuse receptacles, bulk containers or detachable containers shall be determined by the size of the job. Dirt, mud, construction materials or other debris deposited upon any public or private property as a result of construction or demolitions shall be removed by the contractor upon completion of the construction.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 1.14)
Cross reference— Buildings and building regulations, ch. 18.
547:
(a) Contagious disease refuse. The removal of clothing, bedding or other refuse from homes or other places where highly infectious diseases have prevailed shall be performed under the supervision and direction of the county health department. Such refuse shall not be placed in containers for county collection.
(b) Hypodermic instruments. No person shall dispose of or discard any hypodermic syringe, hypodermic needle or any instrument or device for making hypodermic injections before first breaking, disassembling, destroying or otherwise rendering inoperable and incapable of reuse, such hypodermic syringe, needle, instrument or device, and without safeguarding the disposal thereof, by wrapping or securing the syringe in a suitable manner so as to avoid the possibility of causing injury to the collection person.
(c) Cardboard boxes and cartons. Prior to depositing refuse for collection in authorized containers or receptacles or in commercial containers, the person disposing of any such boxes or cartons or the person in charge of the premises shall collapse all cardboard boxes and cartons.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 1.16)
548:
All persons who desire to haul refuse over the county roads shall use a vehicle provided with a cover and operate it so as to prevent refuse from being dropped, blown or spilled.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 1.17)
549:
The owners or agents, tenants or lessees of all residential units and commercial establishments shall be responsible for compliance with this article.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 1.18)
550:
(a) Property. All owners or occupants of property shall maintain their property in a litter-free condition.
(b) Sweeping into sidewalks or streets. No person shall sweep into or deposit in any street or sidewalk the accumulation of litter from any building or property.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 1.19)
551:
It shall be unlawful to abandon any motor vehicle as provided in O.C.G.A. § 36-60-4. Any motor vehicle abandoned within the county shall be disposed of by the proper authorities as provided in O.C.G.A. ch. 36-60.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 2.1)
Cross reference— Traffic and vehicles, ch. 62.
552:
It shall be unlawful for any person to create a nuisance on his property or property occupied by him, or to allow a nuisance to remain on his property or property occupied by him. Dead animals, stagnant water, decayed vegetables or fruits, filthy privies or stables, or anything having an offensive odor, or anything that causes injury or damage to the health or life of any other person are declared nuisances.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 3.1)
553:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to maintain premises, including vacant lots or land, upon which trash, garbage or miscellaneous refuse is permitted or caused to accumulate in any manner which is, or may become, a nuisance, or cause injury to the health or welfare of residents in the vicinity or may injure neighboring property. Drive-in restaurants and other food establishments that permit carry-out food service shall maintain at all times on their premises sufficient receptacles for the disposal of trash, garbage and miscellaneous refuse.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to maintain, cause or permit uncut grass or weeds on any property under such circumstances that the grass or weeds are breeding places for insects, rodents or reptiles or is a fire hazard.
(c) If the person responsible for the conditions described in subsections (a) and (b) of this section has not acted to correct the violation after notice to him by the county administrator, the county administrator, or his agents or designee, may enter upon the premises where the violation occurs and remove the trash, garbage or refuse, or cut the grass or weeds, and the county shall assess costs incurred by it. This shall be a charge against the person responsible, and shall be a lien against the property from which the trash, garbage or refuse was removed, or the grass or weeds were cut.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 3.2)
554:
The county administrator, or the inspector designated by him, shall substantiate complaints of violations of any provisions of this article. They shall determine if there has been a violation and initiate requests for compliance with this article by the person violating this article. The county administrator or his designated inspectors shall be authorized to issue citations against any violator and such citations shall conform to the requirements of O.C.G.A. § 15-10-60 et seq. All violators of this article shall be prosecuted in the magistrate of the county. Upon conviction of a violation hereof the violator shall be punished as provided in section 1-11. The county sheriff, his lawfully appointed deputies, the county administrator or inspector appointed by him shall substantiate complaints of violations of any provisions of this article. The county sheriff, his deputies, or the county administrator or his designated inspector shall be authorized to issue citations against any violator and such citations shall conform to the requirements of O.C.G.A. § 15-10-60 et seq.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 3.3; Res. of 1-13-1987, § 2)
555:
(a) All domestic and other acceptable refuse shall be delivered and deposited at authorized disposal sites in accordance with the directions and orders of the county administrator or his representative in charge of operations, except, however, privately operated sites may be used for the sanitary disposal permits, as required by the regulations of the state department of public health, entitled "solid waste collection and disposal".
(b) All solid waste shall be disposed only at approved disposal sites within the county unless the board of commissioners otherwise grants permission.
(c) An application for permission to transport solid waste to a disposal site outside of the county or to a nonapproved site within the county must be presented to the Crisp County Board of Commissioners on a form supplied by the county landfill operator.
(1) The Crisp County Board of Commissioners shall approve or deny such application upon consideration of the effect of such disposal on the public health and welfare.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 4.1; Ord. No. 2005-1, 4-12-2005)
556:
Public sites approved for the disposal of refuse shall be designated by appropriate signs posted near the roadside at the location of the Cordele-Crisp County Sanitary Landfill. Such sites shall be maintained in use until permanently closed, at which time additional authorized sites shall be opened and publicized by posting of signs and through the press.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 4.2)
557:
Authorized public disposal sites shall be operated Monday through Friday of each week, with the exception of the holidays listed in section 54-148(b), from 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., inclusive. During such hours, acceptable refuse generated in the county shall be received for disposal from any resident of the county.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 4.3)
558:
No person shall enter a disposal site except when an attendant is present and during the hours and days prescribed in section 54-165. All materials delivered and deposited for disposal on the grounds or disposal sites shall be the property of the city of county.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 4.4)
559:
No person shall be permitted to scavenge or reclaim any refuse which has been delivered to a public disposal site for disposal.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 4.5)
560:
(a) Domestic refuse. The following types of refuse shall be classed as "domestic refuse" and shall be accepted for disposal:
(1) Garbage.
(2) Refuse.
(3) Building materials.
(4) Business trash.
(5) Household trash.
(b) Industrial waste. The following types of waste shall be classed as "industrial waste" and shall not be accepted for disposal:
(1) Industrial waste.
(2) Hazardous refuse.
(c) Building materials. Building materials shall be accepted for disposal upon payment of a fee which shall be determined by the director of community development and shall be paid at the time such material is accepted for disposal.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 4.6)
561:
It shall be unlawful for any person to deposit or permit to be deposited on land under his ownership and control any refuse without first having obtained a disposal area permit as required by the regulations of the state department of public health, chapter 170-S-27, entitled "solid waste collection and disposal," and acceptance of the site for such use and purpose by the director of community development.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 4.7)
562:
It shall be the duty and responsibility of the owner of any private disposal site to keep the site in an orderly condition and maintained so as not to be a public nuisance or a menace to public health.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 4.8)
563:
The county administrator, his designated representative, or authorized representative of the department of public health, shall be permitted to enter private disposal sites at any time during normal business hours for free and unhindered inspections to determine compliance with this article and all other pertinent laws and regulations.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 4.9)
564:
(a) No person shall set fire to, or burn any papers or other refuse deposited at any disposal site or on the grounds thereof.
(b) No garbage or other materials, from which offensive odors emanate during combustion, shall be burned outside of any building.
(Res. of 9-9-1986, § 4.10)
567:
The City of Cordele and the county have entered into an intergovernmental agreement providing for, among other things, the county to be the sole owner of and solely responsible for the development and operation of the county landfill, which shall include, without limitation, balefill development and operation. The revenues and expenses of the county landfill have been accounted for as a special revenue fund, as that term is defined by the governmental accounting standards board. The financial director of the county has recommended that the revenues and expenses of the county landfill be accounted for as an enterprise fund, as that term is defined by the governmental accounting standards board. The state department of community affairs has developed a system of accounting (hereafter "full cost accounting system") to help local governments comply with the various reporting requirements of the state's Comprehensive Solid Waste Management Act.
(Res. of 6-14-1996)
568:
(a) Effective July 1, 1996, the costs and revenues of the operation of the county landfill, including any expansion thereof, shall be accounted for as an enterprise fund, which is designated and shall be known as the county landfill enterprise fund.
(b) The full cost accounting system developed by the state department of community affairs is adopted as the system for accounting for the county landfill enterprise fund.
(Res. of 6-14-1996)
570:
This article applies to the preparation, storage, collection, transportation, and disposal of all residential solid waste in the area under the jurisdiction of the county within the unincorporated areas of the county. It prescribes rules and regulations, therefore, regulates the private collection of solid waste, and prohibits the dumping of solid waste within the district.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
571:
For purposes of this article, the following terms shall be defined as follows:
Agreement means any agreement, including exhibits and any amendments thereto, agreed to by the county and the contractor during the term of the agreement.
Bags means plastic sacks furnished by customer designed to store refuse with sufficient wall strength to maintain physical integrity when lifted by top. Total weight of bag and its contents shall not exceed 50 pounds.
Bulky waste means white goods (stoves, freezers, dishwashers, trash compactors, refrigerators, water tanks, washing machines, dryers, water heaters, air conditioners), furniture and other waste materials not included: (construction debris, dead animals, hazardous waste or stable matter) with weights or volumes greater than those allowed for containers. (This item does not include yard waste.)
Bundle means newspapers and magazines securely tied together forming an easily handled package not exceeding 50 pounds in weight. (May be bagged or otherwise containerized in lieu of being tied together.)
Collection equipment means equipment used on a contract which shall not exceed seven years in age.
Commodity means material that can be sold in a spot or future market for processing and use or reuse. Each commodity shall retain its own identity and be kept separate.
Commodity buyer means a buyer or processor of material described in this section.
Construction debris means waste building materials resulting from construction, remodeling, repair or demolition operations.
Container—Solid waste (or roll-out solid waste container) means a roll-out receptacle with a capacity of 90 to 100 gallons constructed of plastic, metal, or fiberglass, having handles of adequate strength for lifting and having a tight fitting lid capable of preventing entrance into the container by vectors. The mouth of a container shall have an opening greater than or equal to that of the base. The containers shall be dark green in color bearing the county's name.
Container—Recyclable materials means a receptacle with a capacity of 18 gallons designed for the purpose of curbside collection of recyclable materials. The receptacle shall be one made of hard plastic and shall be dark green in color.
Contract documents means the request for proposals, instructions to contractors, contractor's proposal, general specifications, the contract performance bond and any addenda or changes to the foregoing documents agreed to by the county and the contractor.
Contractor means the person, corporation, or partnership performing or proposing to perform refuse collection and disposal under contract with the county.
County means the County of Crisp, Georgia or Crisp County, Georgia.
Dead animals means animals or portions thereof that have expired from any cause, except those slaughtered or killed for commercial or human use.
Disposal site means a refuse depository including, but not limited to, municipal solid waste landfills, construction/demolition landfills, transfer stations, incinerators, and waste processing/separation centers licensed, permitted or approved by all governmental bodies and agencies having jurisdiction and requiring such licenses, permits, or approvals to receive for processing or final disposal of refuse and dead animals. The disposal site is the Crisp County landfill. All waste shall be disposed of at this facility by the contractor.
Garbage or putrescible waste means any and all dead animals of less than 20 pounds in weight, except those slaughtered for human consumption; every accumulation of waste (animal, vegetable, and/or other matter) that results from the preparation, processing, consumption, dealing in, handling, packing, canning, storage, transportation, decay or decomposition of meats, fish, fowl, birds, fruits, grains, or other animal or vegetable matter (including, but not by way of limitation, used tin cans, and other food containers; and all putrescible or easily decomposable waste animal or vegetable matter which is likely to attract files or rodents); except (in all cases) any matter included in the definition of bulky waste, construction debris, dead animals, hazardous waste, rubbish, yard waste, or stable matter.
Hazardous waste means waste, in any amount, which is defined, characterized or listed as hazardous by the United States Environmental Protection Agency or appropriate state agency by or pursuant to federal or state law, or waste, in any amount, which is regulated under federal or state law. The term "hazardous waste" shall also include lead acid batteries, acid, fertilizer, bulk insecticides, motor oil, gasoline, and liquid paint.
Producer means an occupant of a residential unit who generates refuse.
Recyclable material(s) means newsprint; aluminum and bi-metal cans; HDPE clear plastic milk jugs, and PET plastic soft drink containers.
Refuse or residential refuse. This term shall refer to residential refuse, rubbish, and bulky waste, construction debris and stable matter generated at a residential unit unless the context otherwise required.
Residential unit means a dwelling within the unincorporated area of Crisp County occupied by a person or group of persons comprising not more than four families. A residential unit may be deemed occupied by the county when either water or domestic light and power services are being supplied thereto. A condominium dwelling, whether of single or multi-level construction, consisting of four or less contiguous or separate single-family dwelling units, shall be treated as a residential unit, except that each single-family dwelling within any such residential unit shall be billed separately as a residential unit.
Rubbish means all waste wood, wood products, chips, shavings, sawdust, printed matter, paper, pasteboard, rags, straw, used and discarded mattresses, used and discarded clothing, used and discarded shoes and boots, combustible waste pulp and other products such as are used for packaging or wrapping crockery and glass, ashes, cinders, floor sweepings, glass, mineral or metallic substances, and any and all other waste materials not included in the definition of bulky waste, construction debris, dead animals, garbage, hazardous waste or stable matter.
Stable matter means all manure and other waste matter normally accumulated in or about a stable, or any animal, livestock, or poultry enclosure, and resulting from the keeping of animals, poultry, or livestock.
Yard waste means leaves, brush, grass, clippings, shrub and tree prunings, discarded Christmas trees, nursery and greenhouse vegetative residuals, and vegetative matter resulting from landscaping maintenance other than mining, agricultural, and silva cultural operations. Yard waste may be bundled, stacked, or bagged. The maximum size on yard waste will be limbs less than three inches in diameter and three feet long. This item does not include land clearing debris.
White goods means freezers, dishwashers, trash compactors, refrigerator, stoves, water tanks, water heaters, washers, dryers, and similar items.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
572:
The board of commissioners hereby finds that the public health of the citizens of the county would be adversely affected should individual citizens be allowed to dispose of solid waste upon their own private property. The board of commissioners finds that it would be in the public interest for the board to pass an ordinance further regulating garbage and solid waste collection and disposal in the district.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
573:
The boundaries of the district shall be all of the property situate, lying and being in the unincorporated areas of the county.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
574:
All fees imposed herein below within the district shall be used and appropriated to pay the cost of collection, storage and/or disposal service within the district, and the necessary related expenses associated therewith by the county, franchisee, contractor collector, or county's designee, including, but not limited to, the purchase of solid waste collection, storage, and/or disposal vehicles, trailers and other equipment; the construction and operation of solid waste collection, storage, and/or disposal collection and/or transfer stations; transportation costs to the disposal site and/or transfer site; tipping fees and disposal charges; and such other costs and expenses as may be deemed needed from time to time by the board of commissioners in order to collect, store and/or dispose of solid waste generated within the district.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
575:
It shall be the duty of both the occupant and owner of every residential unit located in the district to keep all solid waste generated by each such residential unit, pending collection and disposal by the county, franchisee, contract collector, or county's designee, as follows:
(1) Solid waste shall be free from excessive liquid and placed in plastic bags, containers, or bundles or roll-out solid waste container. One 90—100-gallon roll-out solid waste container shall be provided to each residential unit by the county, franchisee, contract collector, or county's designee for use by that residential unit only, for solid waste storage and disposal purposes.
(2) Solid waste shall be bagged and placed in the roll-out solid waste container. Such containers must be kept clean by the residential unit. Yard waste consisting of leaves and grass clippings shall be placed in bags for collection and disposal. Solid waste containers must be placed at curbside by 5:00 a.m. on regular collection days or on the next collection day, if the regular collection day falls on a holiday.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
576:
(a) The county shall have the exclusive right to collect and dispose of all residential solid waste within the district either through employees of the county, franchisee, contract collector, or county's designee issued to a person engaged in the business of residential solid waste collection and disposal. No person shall collect or dispose of any residential solid waste within the district except as provided for herein and except with the express permission of the county. Any waste carried directly to the Crisp County landfill must be tarped or otherwise covered to prevent litter and debris from leaving the vehicle.
(b) The county, franchisee, contractor collector, or county's designee will collect solid waste within the district under the following conditions:
(1) Garbage will be collected once each week from residential unit. Yard waste shall be collected from each residential unit two times per month on regularly scheduled days.
(2) The county, franchisee, contract collector, or county's designee may decline to collect:
a. Garbage and rubbish contained in containers larger than 100 gallons;
b. Any containers that contain excessive liquid; or
c. Any garbage or rubbish not properly placed on the collection day.
(3) The county shall not be responsible for collection of:
a. Construction debris;
b. Commercial solid waste; or
c. Bulky waste.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
577:
(a) The fees for collection of residential solid waste levied pursuant to the terms of this article, and all late charges accruing thereon are hereby levied severally against the owner and occupant of each residential unit, including all residential units located in mobile home courts and/or trailer courts.
(b) The fees and late charges, prescribed in this section shall constitute a continuing lien against the real property upon which each residential unit is located; on the personal property composing a residential unit, and upon the personal property of the occupant of each residential unit, until paid.
(c) The fees and late charges, prescribed in this section shall be billed in the following manner: Each residential unit or premises shall be billed by separate bill. Failure to pay the aforesaid sanitation services shall result in the collection of the aforesaid fees by any and all legal remedies available to the county.
(d) The monthly fees for solid waste collection hereby levied shall be due and payable as instructed on the bills, and if the same are not paid by 60 days after the due date, there is hereby levied a late charge equal to 25 percent of the amount due.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
578:
The fees for the collection and disposal of residential solid waste within the district shall be established from time to time by action of the board of commissioners.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
580:
The county, franchisee, contract collector, or county's designee shall prepare and mail to each residential unit in the district, a quarterly bill showing the amounts of the monthly installments due in advance for residential solid waste collection services. These statements shall be prepared quarterly in advance and each quarterly payment shall be paid in advance by the owner or occupant of each residential unit. A late payment penalty shall be imposed upon each account for which payment is not made within the time limits prescribed thereon. Service may be terminated to accounts not paid within 30 days after the due date. Accounts remaining unpaid more than 60 days after the due date are subject to penalties as provided in section 54-221 herein.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
581:
(a) Whenever the owner or occupant of a residential unit from which solid waste is collected by the county, franchisee, contract collector, or county's designee authorizes or permits the use of private driveways or other portions of private property for such collection, such authorization or permission, whether express or implied, shall be deemed to constitute a waiver on the part of the owner or occupant of the residential unit of any claim for damages against the county, its officers, agent, employees, franchisees, and contractors which result from the use of such private property in the collection process.
(b) The county or any person or entity acting as its franchisee, contract collector, or county's designee pursuant to franchise or contract shall be deemed to have been invited and authorized to enter upon private property for the purpose of collection of solid waste in those cases where other than curbside collection has been requested by the owner or occupant of a residential unit and approved by the county, franchisee, contract collector, or county's designee.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
582:
The owner and occupant of each residential unit, including residential units located in mobile home courts and trailer courts, shall dispose of solid waste only by means of a collection and disposal service provided by the county, franchisee, contract collector, or county's designee.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
583:
Whenever a residential unit becomes vacant, destroyed by fire or other casualty, or is demolished or for some other similar reason no longer generates solid waste, it is incumbent severally upon the owner and former occupant of such residential unit to notify the county of the same. The county may cause such investigation of the report as it deems appropriate and if the county finds the same to be consistent with the provisions hereof, the residential unit in question shall be removed from the solid waste collection list and the fee charge shall thereupon cease. Until such notice shall have been received by the county, however, the fee shall continue to be charged and shall continue to be collectible, notwithstanding the fact that service is not in fact rendered to the residential unit. Similarly, if service has been discontinued pursuant to a notice as provided in this section, but is thereafter resumed, or if land which previously vacant has been improved with a residential unit and begins to receive service, it shall be incumbent on the owner and occupant, severally, to notify the county of such commencement of or resumption of service. The fee prescribed in this article shall be payable for such property from and after the date of resumption of service, whether or not notice has been received.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
584:
The county may charge a fee for resumption of service to the owner and/or occupant of a residential unit where service has been previously discontinued. The amount of such fee shall be that as set from time to time by the board of commissioners.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
585:
It shall be unlawful for any person to dump or bury or cause to be dumped or buried any garbage, refuse, solid waste, or rubbish anywhere in the area of the district not previously approved by the appropriate state authorities.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
586:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to willfully and intentionally violate any of the provisions of this article.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any person willfully and with intent to defraud the county, to evade or defeat or attempt to evade or defraud any fee, penalty, or interest due the county or the payment thereof, imposed by this article.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
587:
It shall be unlawful for any person to burn or attempt to burn or cause to be burned any material of any nature in any container belonging to or used by the county, franchisee, contract collector, or county's designee for residential solid waste collection purposes.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
588:
Each violation of any of the provisions of this article shall be punishable as provided in section 1-11 of this Code. Violations may be tried upon citations with or without a prosecuting attorney as well as upon accusations, as provided in O.C.G.A. § 15-10-6, et seq. Citations shall be issued by the sheriff's department or its designee. Service upon corporations, partnerships, or other entities and organizations shall be affected by serving any managing agent located in the county, or by serving the registered agent, or any officer or partner of the corporation, partnership, organization or entity. The provisions of this article may also be enforced through the use of other remedies, such as injunctive relief, provided by the laws of this state.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
590:
Whenever a corporation, partnership, organization or other entity shall violate any of the provisions of this article such violations shall be deemed to be also that of the individual directors, officers, or agents of such corporation, partnership, organization or other artificial entity who shall have authorized, ordered or done any of the acts constituting in whole or in part such violation. In such cases, service shall also be made upon the individual director, officer, or other agent accused of authorizing, ordering, or doing acts constituting in whole or in part violations of this article.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
591:
The owner, occupant, tenant, or lessee of each residential unit shall, no later than 5:00 a.m. on the normal pickup days designated by the county, franchisee, contract collector, or county's designee, place the containers at the location established by the county, franchisee, contract collector, or county's designee for pickup. Containers shall be removed from the location to the premises of the owner, occupant, tenant or lessee of each such residential unit no later than 24 hours after pickup on the normal day of pickup, subject only to the exceptions enumerated in section 54-225.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
592:
The following are excepted from section 54-224.
(1) Any person with documented disabilities, because of age or physical condition, living in a residential unit where there is no resident or occupant thereof physically capable of placing the container at the designated pickup location shall notify the county and if the county shall find that there is no one in or upon the residential unit on a regular basis physically capable of placing the container at the designated pickup location, then the county may arrange for the solid waste to be picked up at the place on the premises of the residential unit where the container is maintained by the occupant.
(2) The county may establish exceptions for designated residential unit which are determined to be unsuitable for curbside pickup, taking into consideration the terrain, features or other physical impediments, and at such premises, pickup service shall be provided to residential units as determined by the county; or in the alternative, the occupant may be instructed to place only plastic; securely tied bags at a designated location on a scheduled pickup days.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
593:
The roll-out solid waste container furnished by the county, franchisee, contract collector, or county's designee shall not be removed from the premises of the residential unit to which they are delivered and it shall be the duty of the occupant of the residential unit, if the dwelling is to be vacated by the occupant, to notify the county seven days prior to the vacancy.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
594:
If a container previously furnished by the county, franchisee, contract collector, or county's designee to any residential unit is damaged, destroyed, or stolen, it shall be the duty of the owner or occupant of the residential unit to immediately notify the county and to cooperate with the board of commissioners and the county sheriff in investigating the cause of the damage, destruction, or theft. Further, the owner or occupant shall, if requested to do so, appear in the appropriate court as a witness should a prosecution result from the investigation. A replacement container shall be furnished to the residential unit and such unit may be charged a replacement fee as determined by the county.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
595:
Additional containers may be obtained by each residential unit upon payment of an additional monthly fee to the county, franchisee, contract collector, or county's designee as may be set from time to time by the board of commissioners.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
596:
It shall be unlawful for any person to willfully and intentionally damage or destroy or to allow or permit damage to or destruction of any container provided by the county, its franchisee, contract collector, or county's designee.
(Ord. of 7-9-2013; Ord. of 8-2-2013)
598:
Footnote 1:
Cross reference— Any ordinance providing for local improvements and assessing taxes for such improvements saved from repeal, § 1-6(9); any ordinance levying or imposing taxes not included in this Code saved from repeal, § 1-6(14); administration, ch. 2; finance, § 2-221 et seq.; businesses, ch. 22.
600:
The board of commissioners does hereby approve the following policies relative to the correction of errors in the Crisp County tax records and the making of adjustments as to taxes, penalties, and interest due by taxpayers, so long as, in the case of claims, said claims are made within three years of the date of the payment of the tax, penalty or interest, as follows:
(1) Uncollectible bills for taxes due on personal property and prebilled mobile homes that are no longer located within Crisp County, and where neither property nor the taxpayer can be located within the state and made subject to levy or garnishment, shall be added to the insolvency list by the tax commissioner, which list shall be submitted to the governing authority under oath at least annually to be approved by the governing authority and placed in the minutes so as to authorize the purging of such uncollectible accounts from the tax commissioner's digest. Upon approval by the board of commissioners, the tax commissioner shall send a copy of the insolvency list to the board of assessors, in order to remove such accounts from future digests.
(2) Obvious clerical errors in the Crisp County tax records may be corrected by the board of assessors with such officers thereafter reporting such changes or corrections to the board of commissioners and to the respective taxing authorities.
(3) In a disputed case where there is no obvious error, the board of assessors shall forward a recommendation for approval or non-approval to the board of commissioners, and shall provide the information set forth at subsection (4) hereof.
(4) Any and all adjustments, other than those specified hereinabove, shall be submitted by the tax commissioner and board of assessors to the board of commissioners with the recommendations for the relief (if any) to be granted whether it is the forgiveness of tax, penalty or interest or the refund of any such items. Each such request shall be accompanied by a claim for refund or cancellation form, with a sufficient statement of circumstances so as to convey to the commission the reasons for the requested adjustment.
(5) For adjustments set out in subsection (2) of this section, the board of assessors shall forward the forms to the tax commissioner's office for change. For adjustments set out in subsection (3), the board of assessors office shall forward the forms to the board of commissioners. After the decision of the board of commissioners pursuant to subsection (3) or (4), the forms shall be returned to the board of assessors' office for adjustments (if any) for future digests and to the tax commissioner for notification to the taxpayer.
(Res. of 2-8-2005)

603:
In accordance with O.C.G.A. § 48-6-93, there is levied for the year 1984, and for each year thereafter, an annual business license tax upon all depository financial institutions located within the county at a rate of 0.25 percent of the gross receipts of the depository financial institutions. Gross receipts shall mean gross receipts as defined in O.C.G.A. § 48-6-93. Depository financial institution shall mean state and national banks, state building and loan associations, and federal savings and loan associations.
(Ord. of 10-11-1983, § 1)
604:
The minimum annual amount of business license tax due from any depository financial institution, pursuant to section 58-31, shall be $1,000.00.
(Ord. of 10-11-1983, § 2)
605:
Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-6-93(c), each depository financial institution subject to the tax required by this article shall file a return of its gross receipts with the board of commissioners on March 1 of the year following the year in which such gross receipts are measured. The return shall be in the manner and in the form prescribed by the commissioner of the department of revenue based on the allocation method set forth in O.C.G.A. § 48-6-93(d). The board of commissioners shall assess and collect the tax levied pursuant to this article based upon the information provided in the return.
(Ord. of 10-11-1983, § 3)
606:
Taxes levied pursuant to this article shall be due no later than 30 days after filing of the return prescribed by section 58-33 unless extended by the board of commissioners.
(Ord. of 10-11-1983, § 4)
607:
The office of the board of tax assessors of the county is designated as the office to administer the assessment and collection of the taxes levied pursuant to this article. The chief appraiser of the county is directed to forward a copy of this article to each depository financial institution in the county and to the home office of each such depository financial institution if located outside the county.
(Ord. of 10-11-1983, § 5)

610:
Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-5-48.2, there shall be exempt from taxation 100 percent of the value of the tangible personal properties set forth in this section unless changed by further resolution of the board of commissioners:
(1) Inventory of goods in the process of manufacture or production which shall include all partly finished goods and raw materials held for direct use or consumption in the ordinary course of the taxpayer's manufacturing or production business in the state. 613:
A joint sales and use tax at the rate of one percent is levied pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-8-82 effective January 1, 1980.
(Res. of 11-15-1979)
616:
There is authorized to be levied and collected within the county an additional sales and use tax in the amount of one percent on all sales and uses as provided in O.C.G.A. § 48-8-110 et seq. for a period of 20 consecutive calendar quarters commencing on the date of the expiration of the sales and use tax currently in effect.
(Res. of 5-9-2000)

618:
Footnote 4:
Editor's note— Ord. of 1-12-2016 amended Art. VI in its entirety to read as herein set out. Former Art. VI, §§ 58-161—58-168, pertained to hotel-motel excise tax and derived from Res. of 1-12-1988, §§ a—i, k—m; Res. of 2-8-1988.
